strategy_objective_guidance:
- Single scored term: `combined_score = target_ratio * validity`, where `target_ratio = sum(radii)/2.635` and `validity ∈ {0,1}` is a hard gate. Effectively the objective is just the sum of 26 radii, all-or-nothing on validity.
- Validity constraints (tolerance 1e-6): no NaN, radii ≥ 0, every circle inside the unit square (x±r, y±r within [0,1]), and no pairwise overlap (dist ≥ r_i + r_j − 1e-6). Shapes must be exactly (26,2) and (26,).
- No reward for runtime (only a ~350 s hard timeout), determinism, elegance, or reported_sum accuracy (mismatch is only a warning). No partial credit for near-valid packings — an overlap of 1e-5 zeroes the entire score.
- The whole problem is one lever: maximize Σr subject to hard geometric constraints. There is no tradeoff between sub-scores; the only risk is validity failure. Scores above 1.0 are possible (target 2.635 is not a cap).
- Complete input is known in advance: the program receives nothing at runtime; n=26 and the unit square are fixed. This is a fully offline, deterministic construction problem — the constructor may embed a precomputed/painstakingly optimized layout, or run a long offline-style optimization *inside* the constructor (up to ~350 s) and emit the final centers/radii. Nothing forces a "pure explicit formula"; a constructor that internally runs batch optimization and then outputs explicit arrays is fully compliant and typically scores higher.
- Note the 1e-6 slack: solutions can be tightened to exactly touch constraints with a safety margin ~1e-7, and a common failure mode is optimizing right up to the tolerance and tripping it. Always re-validate inside the program and shrink/repair before returning.
strategy_diverge_guidance:
- Known-best layout transcription: hardcode the published best-known n=26 packing (centers/radii from packomania / Erich Friedman tables), scaled to the unit square; pure numpy constants. Mechanism: starts at or near score >1.0 with zero search cost. Verify with the same tolerance as the evaluator.
- Offline nonlinear optimization inside the constructor: treat centers and radii as 78 variables, maximize Σr with scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP or trust-constr) using constraint dicts for all 26·25/2 pairwise distances plus boundary constraints; scipy.optimize.minimize: method='SLSQP', method='trust-constr'. Mechanism: directly optimizes the scored quantity under the exact evaluator constraints; the 350 s budget permits a full solve at runtime.
- Multi-start stochastic search: random or lattice initializations followed by scipy.optimize.differential_evolution or scipy.optimize.dual_annealing on a penalized objective (Σr − λ·violations), then a final feasible projection. Mechanism: escapes the symmetric local optima that hexagonal hand layouts get stuck in.
- Structural constructor families (distinct geometries, not one family): (a) curved-chain / "s" arrangements of near-equal circles along the square's diagonal with corner fillers; (b) mixed-radius shell layout — one large central circle, rings of smaller circles, corner circles; (c) row/column lattice with alternating radii (large-small-large) tuned per row. Each gives a different parametric family whose few parameters (radii per row, offsets) can be optimized by scipy.optimize.minimize.
- LP/SOCP-style feasibility-and-growth iteration: iteratively solve for a common radius scale factor s such that scaled layout (s·r_i) is feasible, using scipy.optimize.brentq on the max-violation function; scipy.optimize: brentq, root. Mechanism: given any fixed contact topology, this finds the exact maximal uniform scaling — a cheap, reliable exploit of any good topology.
strategy_refine_guidance:
- Topology-preserving polish: freeze the contact graph (which circles touch which and which touch walls) and solve the resulting system of quadratic touch equations with scipy.optimize.fsolve / scipy.optimize.root (method='lm'); then verify all gaps ≥ 1e-7. Mechanism: the optimum of any packing is a jammed configuration — solving the exact tangency equations squeezes out the last 1e-3–1e-2 of radius sum.
- Per-circle radius growth loop: repeatedly pick the circle with the largest feasible growth headroom (distance to nearest constraint minus r_i) and grow it by that headroom minus 1e-7; re-solve positions with scipy.optimize.minimize after each growth round. Budget: run until total growth per round < 1e-9 or ~300 s elapsed.
- Perturb-and-repair refinement: random Gaussian perturbation of centers (σ ≈ 1e-3), re-solve feasibility with SLSQP (ftol=1e-12, maxiter=1000), accept if Σr increases and validate_packing-equivalent check passes with margin 5e-7. Mechanism: hill-climbing on the exact scored quantity with validity guaranteed by an internal replica of the evaluator's checks.
- Symmetry breaking: take a symmetric candidate, split it into left/right halves with independent radii, re-optimize; edge effects mean asymmetric packings often beat symmetric ones by ~1e-3.
- Safety-margin calibration: after optimization, compute min over all constraints of (slack), and uniformly shrink all radii by max(0, −min_slack) + 1e-7 so the evaluator's 1e-6 tolerance is never triggered; cost in score is ~2.6e-6, negligible versus a zeroed score.
- Warm-start portfolio: run 2–3 of the divergent families above in-process (each ~60–100 s with scipy.optimize), keep the best validated result, and hardcode the winning layout as a fallback constant so the program is robust to optimizer flakiness within the timeout.

strategies.title: [slsqp-multistart] Full 78-variable constrained optimization with deterministic
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: direct nonlinear constrained optimization of all centers+radii
Replacement scope: Replace `construct_packing`'s hexagonal layout generation and the entire `compute_max_radii` function with a single scipy SLSQP solve over 78 variables (26 x, 26 y, 26 r), objective −Σr, constraints: for each pair (i,j): (x_i−x_j)²+(y_i−y_j)² − (r_i+r_j)² ≥ 0; for each circle: x−r ≥ 0, y−r ≥ 0, 1−x−r ≥ 0, 1−y−r ≥ 0. Multistart from (a) the incumbent hex layout with radii 0.09, (b) a perturbed hex layout, (c) a jittered 5×5+1 grid. Keep the best validated result; fall back to the incumbent hex construction if SLSQP fails.
Compute budget: ≤3 starts × maxiter 300 SLSQP iterations, ftol 1e-12; expected evaluation time well under 60 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's greedy pairwise-scaling radii computation is provably suboptimal (it shrinks both circles of a touching pair even when only one is constrained, and never moves centers); joint optimization of positions and radii unlocks the gap between the current 1.587 and the known ~2.6 region. Expected-gain check: any SLSQP solution with Σr > 1.5869 strictly beats the incumbent's sum_radii; the hex seed with r=0.095 uniform is already feasible with Σr=2.47, so the optimizer starts above the incumbent's objective and can only improve it.

strategies.title: [greedy-growth] Topology-free greedy per-circle radius growth with position re-s
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: iterative growth loop (exploitation of a fixed layout)
Replacement scope: Replace `compute_max_radii` with a growth loop: initialize all radii to a small feasible value (e.g., 0.05) on the incumbent centers, then repeatedly (1) for each circle compute its headroom = min over walls and neighbors of (constraint distance − r_i), (2) grow the circle with the largest headroom by (headroom − 1e-7), (3) every ~10 growth steps re-run a short SLSQP position-only solve (52 variables, radii frozen) to let centers drift away from contacts. Terminate when per-round growth < 1e-9 or 200 s elapse.
Compute budget: growth loop unbounded iterations but capped by 200 s wall clock; position re-solves ≤ 20 × maxiter 200; expected total < 250 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's proportional pairwise scaling loses radius mass whenever a constrained circle is scaled down along with its neighbor; the greedy loop grows only the circle with slack, so total radius is monotonically non-decreasing and strictly increases whenever any circle has headroom. Expected-gain check: starting from the incumbent's radii (Σr = 1.5869), any circle with positive headroom yields strict increase; since the incumbent's greedy scaling leaves visible gaps in the dropped-circle corner region, headroom > 0 exists by construction, so Σr > 1.5869 is guaranteed after one round.

strategies.title: [shell-construction] Mixed-radius shell layout: one large center circle, ring, a
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: structural seed with heterogeneous radii (escape from equal-radius hex ceiling)
Replacement scope: Replace the hexagonal row generation inside `construct_packing` with a parametric shell family: circle 1 at (0.5, 0.5) with radius a; 8 circles on a ring of radius a+b at angles k·45° with radius b; 4 corner circles at (c,c),(1−c,c),(c,1−c),(1−c,1−c) with radius c; 4 edge-midpoint circles at (0.5,c),(0.5,1−c),(c,0.5),(1−c,0.5); the remaining 9 circles as a second partial ring of radius a+3b at angles k·30° (k=0..8) with radius b. Optimize the 3 parameters (a, b, c) plus ring angles with scipy minimize on the max-violation, then run the greedy growth loop from Strategy 2 on the resulting layout.
Compute budget: parameter optimization ≤ 50 starts × 200 iterations (3–15 variables, fast); growth loop capped at 150 s; expected total < 200 s.
Gain mechanism: The equal-radius hex lattice cannot exploit the square's corners and center simultaneously — corner regions are wasted at radius 0.1 when they could hold circles of radius up to ~0.207 (corner circle inscribed at 45°). Heterogeneous radii let large circles occupy the center and corners while small circles fill interstices, which is exactly the structure of the known 2.635 solution. Expected-gain check: a feasible member of this family with a=0.18, b=0.09, c=0.12 (verifiable by direct distance checks) already gives Σr ≈ 0.18+12·0.09+4·0.12 = 1.86 > 1.5869, and the growth loop only increases it.

strategies.title: [diagonal-chain] Curved S-chain of near-equal circles along the diagonal with co
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: diagonal-chain-seed
Replacement scope: add `_chain_seed()` and insert it as the top-priority seed in `construct_packing()`'s `seeds` list; keep the incumbent hex/shell seeds and SLSQP `_run` machinery unchanged.
Compute budget: no new optimizer; one extra SLSQP start (maxiter 400) added to the existing ≤7-start loop, expected evaluation-time increase ≈ +2–3 s.
Gain mechanism: the incumbent's seeds are all hexagonal/ring lattices, whose equal-radius ceiling for 26 circles in a unit square is Σr ≈ 26·(1/(2·5))·(≈0.97) ≈ 2.52–2.58; the best-known packings for n≈25–30 in a square use a curved "S"-shaped chain of touching near-equal circles running corner-to-corner with smaller circles filling the two remaining corners. Construction: place 18 circles of radius r≈0.095 as a staggered chain following two arcs (centers on the curve y = 0.5 + 0.35·sin(π·(x−0.1)/0.8), sampled at arc-length spacing 2r·0.99), plus 4 corner circles of radius ≈0.065 at (r',r')-type positions, plus 4 edge-midpoint circles ≈0.08 — a genuinely different contact topology (chain-of-contacts rather than triangular lattice) that SLSQP then relaxes. Validity is preserved because every candidate still passes through the existing `_feasible` gate with the incumbent fallback retained.
Expected-gain check: the chain topology has a strictly larger uniform-radius bound (18·0.095 + 4·0.065 + 4·0.08 = 2.53 before relaxation, versus the hex seed's 26·0.0985 = 2.56 frozen lattice that SLSQP cannot leave), and after SLSQP relaxation of the chain's 78 free variables the local optimum is a different basin; the falsifiable threshold is combined_score > 0.977261 (Σr > 2.5751) on the evaluator.

strategies.title: [row-alternating] Per-row alternating large/small radius lattice with independen
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: row-alternating-lattice
Replacement scope: replace `_shell_seed()` (its mixed-ring layout plateaus) with `_row_seed()` producing the layout, and feed it as the primary seed in `construct_packing()`; keep `_hex_seed` as fallback.
Compute budget: Nelder–Mead on ≤5 structural parameters (row y-offsets, two radii values, per-row x-offset), ≤8 starts × maxiter 300, then the existing single SLSQP start from the result; expected total ≈ +4 s.
Gain mechanism: instead of one global radius, use rows of alternating radii: rows 1,3,5 hold 5 circles of radius a, rows 2,4 hold 4 circles of radius b>a placed in the gaps of adjacent rows (x-offset by half-spacing), plus 2 extra circles in the widest residual pockets; the degree of freedom the incumbent lacks is that small circles in row gaps let the large circles be larger than the uniform hex limit — the per-row spacing for radius-a circles can exceed 2a because the b-circles occupy the interstitial gaps, and the five structural parameters are fit to the actual square boundary rather than forced into a symmetric lattice. Wall constraint: each row's y is chosen so y−a (or y−b) ≥ 0 and y+a ≤ 1, enforced inside the constructor before SLSQP.
Expected-gain check: with a=0.105, b=0.075 the raw layout already gives 5·3·0.105 + 2·4·0.075 + 2·0.075 = 2.145 from the alternating rows alone plus 2 pocket circles ≈ 2·0.09 → Σr ≈ 2.33 pre-relaxation with substantial SLSQP headroom in the 5 free row parameters; the falsifiable evaluator threshold is Σr > 2.5751 (combined_score > 0.977261), with the incumbent fallback guaranteeing no regression below the current score.

strategies.title: [jammed-polish] Contact-graph freezing + per-circle greedy growth with uniform-s
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: jammed-contact-polish
Replacement scope: replace the 4-iteration "bounded refinement" loop at the end of `construct_packing()` with a two-phase polish: (i) per-circle greedy growth, (ii) brentq uniform rescale.
Compute budget: growth loop ≤ 40 passes, each pass is O(26²) numpy distance checks (no optimizer); brentq with xtol 1e-12, ≤60 function evals; expected +1–2 s, no new SLSQP starts.
Gain mechanism: SLSQP stops at ftol 1e-12 with constraints still having positive slack for many circles (the current output is not jammed). Phase (i): for each circle i compute headroom h_i = min(min-wall-slack, min_j(dist_ij − r_i − r_j)) and grow r_i by h_i − 5e-7 (iterating because growing one circle may shrink another's headroom; accept a pass only if Σr increases, else stop). Phase (ii): after growth, find the exact maximal uniform scale s* via brentq on the max-violation function g(s) = max over pairs/walls of (required − actual distance) for radii s·r, then set r ← (s* − 5e-7/scale)·r. This extracts the residual 1e-3–1e-2 of radius sum SLSQP leaves on the table while the 5e-7 margin keeps every constraint strictly inside the evaluator's 1e-6 tolerance; the incumbent fallback (`best_c, best_r`) is returned unchanged if any intermediate state fails `_feasible` with margin.
Expected-gain check: the incumbent's SLSQP solutions typically carry ≥1e-3 total slack across 26 circles (ftol 1e-12 on a Σr ≈ 2.58 objective leaves per-circle slack ~1e-4–1e-5 each), so the predicted Σr gain is ≈ +2e-3–1e-2, i.e. combined_score ≈ 0.978–0.981 > 0.977261, and the falsifiable threshold is a strict increase of Σr over the incumbent with validity=1 on the evaluator.
